contract: Caller-owned JSON Schema checking bound to exact Port direction, schema ID and version; original JSON payload retained, compact encoding at most 65,536 bytes and container depth at most 32; failures return fixed tags or at most 16 key-redacted structural violations.
limits: Host-approved decoded schema objects only, draft 2020-12, fragment-only references; conservative scanning also refuses reserved reference keys in literal schema data.
Bounds cover accepted payloads and returned violations, not encoding allocation, validator errors, regex/schema complexity, CPU or memory.
No schema registry, digest, negotiation, defaults, coercion, codec, process, persistence, effects or delivery guarantee; ready callers keep their existing admission and disagreement policy.
No exhaustive violation list, total count or ordering guarantee; structural paths are not dereferenceable JSON Pointers.
ex_json_schema and telemetry are declared for copied tests, not production validation. Snapshot comparison is a repository-only observation recorded in README, not copied runtime support.

grounding.claim: Named declared-type, malformed-shape, reference, unknown-field, size/depth, violation-bound, version/binding, redaction/log/event, pinned-validator divergence and checked-example scenarios; finite tests, not a universal proof.
Pinned build and cast:false validation with resolver:[], formats:false, atoms:false and warnings silenced; Error.data_path is reversed, with binary object keys and integer array positions.
Default compact JSON encoding supplies the byte count after representation and depth checks.

The host supplies truthful Port identities, consistent schema meaning per ID/version pair and approved schema complexity. Checked values come from build/2; forged internals are outside the Contract. Port descriptor policy relies on the unchanged core/port dependency and its pinned Cure grounding.

telemetry.contract: No logs or telemetry emitted; the caller owns instrumentation.

config.contract: Intrinsic Port/schema/payload operands and fixed bounds; no selectable settings.

control.contract: Caller-owned immutable schema state only; no process or lifecycle commands.
